target.title: fix(gateway): worker workspaces recover after stalled process probes
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cloud worker workspace sessions could remain quiesced
indefinitely when the detached expiry watchdog's process identity probe stalled
and did not exit after `SIGTERM`. Because the parent SSH command had already
returned, no outer command deadline remained to release the lease.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detached watchdog now runs its `ps` identity probe asynchronously with a
one-second deadline. When that deadline expires, it closes the probe pipes,
force-terminates and unreferences the child, and retries the full lease check
without waiting for the probe to exit. PID start-time matching remains required
before `SIGCONT`, so recovery does not weaken process identity safety.

## User Impact

Expired cloud worker workspace leases can recover even when a host process probe
ignores normal termination. Identity-matched frozen processes resume and the
lease is removed instead of leaving the workspace unavailable indefinitely.
There are no config, schema, protocol, or migration changes.

## Evidence

- Node.js 24 documents that `execFileSync()` still waits for a timed-out child
  that handles or ignores `SIGTERM`, confirming why the prior synchronous
  timeout could not enforce the watchdog deadline.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-sync-scripts.test.ts`
  - 1 test file passed
  - 9 tests passed
  - Includes a regression whose first `ps` process records its PID, ignores
    `SIGTERM`, and sleeps; the watchdog must retry and release the lease.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ...`, targeted `oxlint`, and
  `git diff --check` passed for both changed files.
- Near-real owner-runtime proof executed the production generated quiescence
  script with a real detached watchdog, real lease persistence, and a real
  POSIX target process:
  - heartbeat bytes before/while stopped: `3 -> 3`
  - first identity probe ignored `SIGTERM`
  - lease removed and target resumed in 3.778 seconds
  - heartbeat bytes after release: `4`

### Proof boundary

The runtime proof uses real processes and `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT` on a local Linux
host. Only `ps` is replaced to inject one deterministic signal-resistant stall.
This is not a hosted cloud-worker run, so provider-host-specific process behavior
remains an external proof gap.
